channel.title: Credit4Vets — Insights
channel.description: Credit, housing, business, and benefits information for those who served — from a veteran-founded nonprofit in Tempe, Arizona.

item.title: Your first civilian paycheck: what changes after you separate
item.description: A civilian salary that looks bigger than military pay can leave you with less. Here's what changes in your paycheck after separation and what to do first.

item.title: Holiday spending without the January debt
item.description: The holidays are when a lot of new debt gets taken on, often in small pieces. Here's how to set a plan now and avoid the traps built for this season.

item.title: Arizona resources every veteran should know about
item.description: From free claims help to a new full property tax exemption for 100% disabled veterans, here are the Arizona veteran benefits worth checking.

item.title: Credit freezes, fraud alerts, and protecting yourself from identity theft
item.description: A credit freeze is free, does not hurt your score, and stops most new-account fraud. Here's how it works and when a fraud alert makes more sense.

item.title: How debt-to-income works for a VA home loan
item.description: VA loans look at your debt-to-income ratio and your residual income. Here's how both are measured and what you can do to improve them before you apply.

item.title: Building an emergency fund when money is already tight
item.description: An emergency fund is what keeps a car repair from turning into a payday loan. Here's how to start one, even a small one, and where to keep it.

item.title: Open enrollment season: VA health care, the Marketplace, and Medicare
item.description: Medicare, Marketplace, and TRICARE enrollment windows all open this fall. Here's how each fits with VA health care and which deadlines apply to you.

item.title: How to read a credit card agreement before you sign
item.description: The terms that decide what a credit card actually costs you are in the agreement. Here's where to find them and which ones to read first.

item.title: Budgeting on a fixed VA disability income
item.description: VA disability compensation is steady and predictable, which makes it easier to budget around and easier for others to target. Here's how to build a plan on it.

item.title: How credit scores work, and why you have more than one
item.description: Your credit score is a prediction built from your credit reports. Here's what goes into it, why the numbers differ, and what actually moves them.

item.title: Scams that specifically target veterans
item.description: Veterans are deliberately targeted because benefits are predictable income and service is easy to look up. Here are the patterns worth recognizing.

item.title: Free tax preparation for veterans and military families
item.description: Paid preparers charge for returns that several free programs will handle. Here's what's available and who qualifies.

item.title: Building credit from a thin file
item.description: Not having credit history isn't the same as having bad credit — but lenders often treat it that way. Here's how to build a file from close to nothing.

item.title: The Military Lending Act protects active duty — not veterans
item.description: A 36% rate cap covers you while you serve. It does not follow you out, and predatory lenders know exactly when it stops.

item.title: Writing a business plan when you're coming out of service
item.description: Most business plan advice is written for MBA students. Here's the version for someone whose experience is operational rather than commercial.

item.title: SBA programs built for veteran business owners
item.description: Several federal programs exist specifically for veterans starting or growing a business. Most go underused because nobody hears about them.

item.title: Where to find mental health support as a veteran
item.description: Free, confidential help exists, including for veterans who aren't enrolled in VA health care. Here's what's available and how to reach it.

item.title: Housing help for veterans: where to start
item.description: If you're facing housing instability, there is a single number to call, it's free, and it's staffed around the clock.

item.title: The VA home loan: what makes it different
item.description: One of the strongest benefits earned through service, and one of the most misunderstood. Here's what it actually is.

item.title: Disputing an error on your credit report, step by step
item.description: Filing a dispute is free and you can do it yourself. Here's exactly how, and what to expect afterward.

item.title: What credit repair companies can and can't do for you
item.description: Some are legitimate. Many are not. Here's the law, the warning signs, and what you can do yourself for free.

item.title: How to get your credit reports for free (and why you should)
item.description: You are entitled to free weekly reports from all three bureaus. Here's how to get them without hitting the sites that charge you.
